title: Words Given to Malachi
summary: He commanded them to write the words the Father had given to Malachi. After the words were written, he expounded them and told them words announcing a messenger who would prepare the way and the Lord, called the messenger of the covenant, who would come to his temple.

explicit_facts.text: He commanded them to write the words the Father had given to Malachi, which he would tell them.
After the words were written, he expounded them.
The words he told them announce a messenger preparing the way and the Lord, called the messenger of the covenant, coming to his temple.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The listeners may be shown attending to him as he expounds the already-written words.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities of those who wrote the words.

spoken_dialogue.text: Thus said the Father unto Malachi—Behold, I will send my messenger,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father

spoken_dialogue.text: and the Lord whom ye seek shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in; behold, he shall come, saith the Lord of Hosts.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father

narration.text: And it came to pass that after they were written he expounded them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The command and writing precede the exposition; do not show them as simultaneous.
The messenger and the promised arrival at the temple are part of the words being told, not visible events occurring in this scene.
Narration belongs to Mormon; the recited words are spoken by Jesus Christ and attributed to the Father.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Father, Malachi, or the promised messenger as physically present.
Do not depict the promised temple arrival as occurring in this scene.
Do not invent the content of the exposition or additional dialogue.
Do not assign named writers or present particular writing materials as textual facts.

title: The Words Given to Malachi
summary: Jesus Christ commands them to write the words the Father gave Malachi. After they are written, he expounds them and tells them the words.

explicit_facts.text: He commands them to write the words the Father gave Malachi.
After the words are written, he expounds them.
He tells them words concerning a messenger who will prepare the way and the Lord who will come to his temple.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The commanded group may be shown writing before Jesus Christ expounds the words.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, writing materials, and appearances of those present are not described.

narration.text: And it came to pass that he commanded them that they should write the words which the Father had given unto Malachi, which he should tell unto them.
And it came to pass that after they were written he expounded them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The messenger's preparation and the Lord's coming are spoken prophecy, not events occurring in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the prophesied messenger or an arrival at the temple.
Do not invent the messenger's identity or appearance, or the temple's appearance.
Do not show the writing and expounding happening at the same time.
Do not depict the Father or Malachi as physically present.

title: The Day of His Coming
summary: The prophecy asks who can endure the day of the Lord’s coming, comparing him to refining fire and fuller’s soap, and says he will purify the sons of Levi.

explicit_facts.text: The prophecy asks who may abide the day of his coming and who shall stand when he appears.
He is compared to a refiner’s fire and fuller’s soap, and is said to purify the sons of Levi.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Metaphorical imagery may suggest refining and cleansing without depicting a literal supernatural event.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearances of the Lord and the sons of Levi.

spoken_dialogue.text: who may abide the day of his coming,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father’s words to Malachi

narration.text: he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The fire and soap are figures of speech; do not portray them as literal acts.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal refining scene or invent the Lord’s appearance.

title: An Offering in Righteousness
summary: The prophecy says the sons of Levi will offer in righteousness, and Judah and Jerusalem’s offering will be pleasant to the Lord as in former days.

explicit_facts.text: The sons of Levi are to offer unto the Lord an offering in righteousness.
The offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasant to the Lord as in former years.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic offering may represent the prophecy, without specifying its form.
unspecified_visual_details: The offering’s form, participants’ appearances, and location.

spoken_dialogue.text: that they may offer unto the Lord an offering in righteousness.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father’s words to Malachi

narration.text: Then shall the offering of Judah and Jerusalem be pleasant unto the Lord,

prohibited_inventions: Do not specify a sacrificial rite or portray a distinct historical event.

title: A Swift Witness in Judgment
summary: The prophecy says the Lord will come near to judge and witness against wrongdoing and oppression.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says he will come near to judgment and be a swift witness against sorcerers, adulterers, false swearers, those who oppress hired workers, widows and fatherless people, and those who turn aside strangers and do not fear him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Represent the listed wrongs symbolically rather than inventing specific incidents or people.
unspecified_visual_details: The people involved, setting, and form of judgment.

spoken_dialogue.text: I will come near to you to judgment;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father’s words to Malachi

narration.text: against those that oppress the hireling in his wages,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a prophetic warning, not a narrated present-tense judgment event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray a specific judgment or identify unnamed wrongdoers.

title: The Lord Changes Not
summary: The Lord says he does not change, that the sons of Jacob are not consumed, and that they have departed from his ordinances. He calls them to return to him and reports their question about returning.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says he does not change and that the sons of Jacob are not consumed.
The Lord says those addressed have gone away from his ordinances and have not kept them.
The Lord calls them to return to him and reports their question about returning.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The words can be presented without depicting a visible encounter.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and appearances of those addressed are not specified.
No visible appearance of the Lord is described.

spoken_dialogue.text: For I am the Lord, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: Return unto me and I will return unto you,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: Wherein shall we return?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The people addressed by the Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The people's question is reported by the Lord; do not stage it as a separate present-tense encounter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an appearance of the Lord or invent a setting.
Do not invent individual questioners or additional dialogue.

title: Tithes and Offerings
summary: God says the people have robbed him in tithes and offerings and that the whole nation is cursed because it has robbed him.

explicit_facts.text: God says the people have robbed him in tithes and offerings.
The people ask how they have robbed him.
God says the whole nation is cursed because it has robbed him.

unspecified_visual_details: The location and the people's appearances.

spoken_dialogue.text: Will a man rob God? Yet ye have robbed me.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: God

spoken_dialogue.text: Wherein have we robbed thee?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The people addressed

spoken_dialogue.text: In tithes and offerings.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: God

spoken_dialogue.text: Ye are cursed with a curse, for ye have robbed me, even this whole nation.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The accusation and curse are spoken statements, not narrated visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an act of theft or a visible curse.
Do not invent a setting or a physical appearance for God.

title: Bring the Tithes
summary: The Lord of Hosts commands the people to bring all tithes into the storehouse and promises a blessing if they prove him.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord of Hosts commands that all tithes be brought into the storehouse so there may be meat in his house.
The Lord of Hosts invites the people to prove him and promises to open the windows of heaven and pour out a blessing beyond room to receive it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The storehouse may be suggested symbolically; the verse does not narrate anyone bringing tithes there.
unspecified_visual_details: The storehouse’s appearance and the nature of the promised blessing.

spoken_dialogue.text: Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in my house; and prove me now herewith, saith the Lord of Hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing that there shall not be room enough to receive it.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lord of Hosts

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The blessing is promised, not narrated as occurring.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict heaven opening, invent a specific blessing, or portray the command as an event already carried out.

title: The Fruits of the Ground
summary: The Lord of Hosts promises to rebuke the devourer so it will not destroy the fruits of the ground, and declares that all nations will call the people blessed.
locations: Unspecified setting; fields are mentioned in the promise

explicit_facts.text: The Lord of Hosts says he will rebuke the devourer, which will not destroy the fruits of the ground; the vine will not cast its fruit before its time.
The Lord of Hosts says all nations will call the people blessed and they will be a delightsome land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Fruitful ground and a vine could illustrate the promise without portraying it as an event already occurring.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the appearance of the Lord of Hosts, the land, the devourer, and the nations are not described.

spoken_dialogue.text: And I will rebuke the devourer for your sakes, and he shall not destroy the fruits of your ground; neither shall your vine cast her fruit before the time in the fields, saith the Lord of Hosts.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lord of Hosts

spoken_dialogue.text: And all nations shall call you blessed, for ye shall be a delightsome land, saith the Lord of Hosts.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lord of Hosts

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses state promises, not their fulfillment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the devourer as a visible creature or show the promised events as having occurred.
Do not invent an appearance for the Lord of Hosts or identify the nations.

title: Words Against the Lord
summary: The Lord says the people's words have been stout against him. They ask what they have spoken against him. He reports their claims that serving God is vain, that keeping his ordinances brings no profit, and that the proud are happy, the wicked are set up, and those who tempt God are delivered.
characters: The people whose words are reported

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says the people's words have been stout against him; they ask what they have spoken against him.
The Lord reports that they have called serving God vain and questioned the profit of keeping his ordinances and walking mournfully before him.
They say the proud are happy, those who work wickedness are set up, and those who tempt God are delivered.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The exchange can be conveyed without showing the speakers or staging a new conversation.
unspecified_visual_details: The speakers' appearances and physical setting are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Your words have been stout against me,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: What have we spoken against thee?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The people whose words are reported

spoken_dialogue.text: It is vain to serve God,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The people whose words are reported

spoken_dialogue.text: what doth it profit that we have kept his ordinances and that we have walked mournfully before the Lord of Hosts?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The people whose words are reported

spoken_dialogue.text: And now we call the proud happy;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The people whose words are reported

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The people's words are reported within the Lord's speech, not a newly staged conversation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent individual speakers, a physical appearance for the Lord, or visible acts of wickedness.

title: A Book of Remembrance
summary: Those who feared the Lord spoke often to one another. The Lord heard them, and a book of remembrance was written before him for those who feared him and thought upon his name. The Lord of Hosts says they will be his and he will spare them in a future day.

explicit_facts.text: Those who feared the Lord spoke often to one another, and the Lord heard them.
A book of remembrance was written before the Lord for those who feared him and thought upon his name.
The Lord of Hosts says they will be his when he makes up his jewels and that he will spare them as a man spares his own son who serves him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People may be shown speaking to one another.
A book may be shown being written, without identifying its writer.

spoken_dialogue.text: And they shall be mine,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord of Hosts

spoken_dialogue.text: in that day when I make up my jewels; and I will spare them as a man spareth his own son that serveth him.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord of Hosts

narration.text: Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another,
and the Lord hearkened and heard;
and a book of remembrance was written before him

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Present the verse 16 narration before the Lord's promise in verse 17. The promise concerns a future day; the jewels and father-son comparison are not additional visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent what the people said or identify the writer.
Do not depict literal jewels, a father-and-son event, or an appearance for the Lord.

title: Discern Between the Righteous and the Wicked
summary: Those addressed are told that they will return and discern between the righteous and the wicked, and between those who serve God and those who do not.

explicit_facts.text: Those addressed will return and discern between the righteous and the wicked, and between one who serves God and one who does not.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The future distinction could be conveyed through text or abstract contrast without depicting it as an event already occurring.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of those addressed.
The setting and visual form of the contrast.

spoken_dialogue.text: Then shall ye return and discern between the righteous and the wicked, between him that serveth God and him that serveth him not.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father's words to Malachi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes future discernment, not a judgment occurring in the verse.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unreported judgment or identify particular people as righteous or wicked.
